title: First Capital Financial: Enterprise Context at a Glance
executive_summary: A regulated regional bank with fragmented core, digital, risk, and data estate requiring evidence before AI activation.
what_context_reveals: Seven strategic AI use cases identified; all gated by lineage, auditability, and model-risk evidence needs.
why_it_matters: Control expectations and vendor dependency create compounding risk if AI moves ahead of governance readiness.
decision_implication: No use case is production-ready; all require evidence validation before value claims or deployment decisions.
evidence_still_needed: Lineage certification, model-risk approvals, baseline metrics, and control attestations across all seven use cases.
module_usage: Knowledge module anchors enterprise context; Source module gates vendor and contract decisions pending evidence.
next_validation_action: Prioritize evidence collection for fraud copilot and AML/KYC lineage before any AI deployment sequencing.

title: Regulated Regional Bank with High Control Expectations
executive_summary: First Capital Financial operates across lending, cards, payments, fraud, AML/KYC, and wealth under strong regulatory oversight.
what_context_reveals: Business model is synthetic planning-grade; no real customer, account, or transaction data is claimed or evidenced.
why_it_matters: Regulatory exposure across multiple sub-industries amplifies the cost of ungoverned AI or data decisions.
decision_implication: Enterprise profile demands evidence-first sequencing; transformation hypotheses need compliance and risk co-sign.
evidence_still_needed: Current-state regulatory posture, exam history, and control framework maturity need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module maps enterprise profile to use-case gating criteria and control expectations.
next_validation_action: Request regulatory posture summary and control framework documentation from risk and compliance leadership.

title: Multi-Function Bank with Siloed Operational Domains
executive_summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.
what_context_reveals: Seven use cases span risk, customer experience, operations, and data functions; integration gaps are pervasive.
why_it_matters: Siloed functions prevent unified customer view, complicate AI deployment, and fragment control accountability.
decision_implication: Function-level evidence must precede cross-domain AI initiatives; sequencing risk is high without integration proof.
evidence_still_needed: Cross-function data-sharing agreements, integration architecture, and ownership maps need evidence.
module_usage: Knowledge module surfaces function-level gaps; flags where integration evidence is missing before use-case activation.
next_validation_action: Map data-sharing agreements and integration ownership across lending, fraud, AML, and payments functions.

title: Ownership Accountability Gaps Across Risk and Data Domains
